report:
The evidence on whether coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) relieves statin-associated muscle discomfort is **mixed and inconclusive**, though your instinct of "no" is supported by some of the higher-quality studies.

**Biological rationale:** Statins inhibit the mevalonate pathway, which reduces endogenous CoQ10 production. This led to the hypothesis that supplementation could counteract statin-associated muscle symptoms (SAMS). However, this plausible mechanism has not been consistently validated clinically.

**Key evidence against benefit:**
- A 2015 meta-analysis by Banach et al. of 6 RCTs (302 patients) concluded that results "do not suggest any significant benefit of CoQ10 supplementation in improving statin-induced myopathy" ([Mayo Clinic Proceedings](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002561961400799X)).
- A randomized trial in patients with *confirmed* statin myalgia (the gold-standard design, since many suspected cases turn out to be placebo effects) found no benefit: pain reduction occurred in 53% of CoQ10 recipients vs. 65% of placebo recipients (p=0.43) ([Atherosclerosis, 2015](https://www.atherosclerosis-journal.com/article/S0021-9150(15)01205-8/fulltext)).

**Key evidence suggesting benefit:**
- A 2018 meta-analysis (Qu et al.) found CoQ10 "ameliorated statin-associated muscle symptoms" ([Journal of the American Heart Association](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/full/10.1161/JAHA.118.009835)).
- A 2025 meta-analysis reported a "significant reduction in muscle pain intensity" with CoQ10 ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12554813/)).

**Bottom line:** The evidence is conflicting. The studies showing benefit tend to include patients with *unconfirmed* statin myalgia (where placebo effects and symptom fluctuation are common), while the most methodologically rigorous trial—using a crossover run-in to confirm true statin-associated pain—found no benefit. The Mayo Clinic notes CoQ10 "may help" some people but that "more studies are needed" ([Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/high-blood-cholesterol/in-depth/statin-side-effects/art-20046013)). Overall, CoQ10 is not reliably proven to relieve statin-related muscle discomfort.
